stages.name: Weaknesses of supply-side policy
stages.title: Weaknesses of supply-side policy
stages.sub: After this, the student can explain why supply-side policies are slow and expensive compared with other policy types.

steps.q: A government wants to keep its spending roughly equal to its tax revenue, but it also wants to build a new motorway and fund years of extra training for workers. Can it do this without spending any extra money?
steps.right: No, it must spend a large amount
steps.hint: Think about roads, schools and training courses: are they free to provide?
steps.pre: So building infrastructure and improving skills both require heavy

steps.q: The motorway takes 5 years to build, and it takes a worker years of training to become skilled. Does the economy feel the benefit straight away?
steps.right: No, only after a long period
steps.hint: Can a road be built or a worker be trained overnight?

steps.q: A government announces a skills programme today, hoping it will raise the country's output. If it takes years for workers to actually become more productive, when will the policy's effect on growth actually show up?
steps.hint: The training itself takes years, so when does the productivity gain follow?

steps.q: The government has just spent heavily on new infrastructure and skills training, well beyond what it collects in tax that year. What happens to the gap between government spending and tax revenue?
steps.right: It widens, since spending has risen without matching tax revenue
steps.wrong: It narrows, since the spending boosts tax revenue straight away
steps.hint: Think about the large spending on roads and training: does that money come back in as tax straight away?
